test_title: PYST 03: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct Speech.

She said that she could have passed the exam.

options.text: She said, "I would have passed the exam."
She said, "I could have passed the exam.
She said, "I might have passed the exam."
She said, "I should have passed the exam.”

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she could have passed the exam.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"She said that she could have passed" becomes "She said, 'I could have passed'"**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged.
 
• The pronoun "she" is converted to "I" to match the direct speech perspective.
 
• The modal verb "could have passed" remains the same in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• The quoted speech starts with a capital letter and ends with a period.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said, 'I could have passed the exam.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said, 'I would have passed the exam.'"

 
 
• The modal "would have passed" changes the meaning from possibility (could) to certainty under certain conditions, which is incorrect.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said, 'I might have passed the exam.'"
 
 
• The modal "might have passed" changes the meaning from ability (could) to uncertainty, which alters the original intent.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said, 'I should have passed the exam.'"
 
 
• The modal "should have passed" implies obligation or regret, which is different from the original meaning.
